requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1
requirements.summary: Transit addressing configured on both links, HTTP server on node3:8080 reached with HTTP 200 from node2 both before and after all three restarts.

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 passing between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: nftables forward-hook chain on node1 explicitly rejects tcp dport 23 with tcp reset between eth1/eth2; a listener was confirmed running on node3:23 and curl from node2 got 'Connection refused' consistent with a TCP RST, verified both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Rest of the forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
requirements.summary: Forward chain default policy is accept and only matches tcp dport 8080/23; ICMP ping between node2 and node3 through node1 succeeds both before and after restarts, showing other traffic is not blocked.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Captured boot_id f6f9440e and healthy functional state pre-restart, issued reboot (SSH connection dropped confirming ack), polled until boot_id changed to f56c387b (matches lifecycle after_executor snapshot), then verified addressing, routes, and 8080/23/ping behavior fully recovered.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Captured boot_id 2ba78175 and healthy state pre-restart, issued reboot (SSH connection dropped confirming ack), polled until boot_id changed to 655a975c (matches lifecycle after_executor snapshot), then verified addressing/routes recovered and test listeners re-established successfully.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Captured boot_id 39fdb9ab and healthy state pre-restart, issued reboot (log showed 'requested COLD shutdown', subsequent polling got connection reset/timeout confirming ack), polled through SONiC's multi-container boot until boot_id changed to 27e2c370 (matches lifecycle after_executor snapshot), then verified eth1/eth2 addressing, sysctl forwarding, and the nft ACL table recovered automatically via the enabled systemd unit, followed by an end-to-end functional retest.

requirements.requirement: Configuration persists across reboot rather than only existing as runtime state
requirements.summary: sysctl.d, ifupdown fragments (node2/node3), and an enabled systemd unit plus idempotent nft ruleset file (node1) were installed and confirmed intact/functional after an actual reboot, with no rule duplication on reapplication.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, functional evidence: node2/node3 reach each other on TCP 8080, node1's nft forward-chain rejects TCP 23 between them with a TCP reset, and other forwarded traffic (ICMP) passes untouched via the default-accept policy — all verified both before and after restarting every node. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also fully and correctly executed for all three nodes, each showing a healthy baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full functional recovery, including persistence of the nft ACL and forwarding configuration across node1's more complex SONiC reboot. Hygiene is generally good; the only notable issues are a self-corrected nft rule-duplication mistake, an under-justified docker0 address/interface mutation on node1, and small leftover log files from test HTTP servers on node3.
limitations: The 'other traffic untouched' outcome was only directly tested with ICMP; no other protocols/ports besides 8080 and 23 were exercised end-to-end, though this is reasonable given the accept-by-default policy shown in the ruleset.

Whether removing docker0's address and disabling interfaces-config.service on node1 was strictly necessary for the routing/ACL outcome versus optional cleanup could not be fully determined from the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites (interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, nft ACL, persistence files) or bounded/cleaned-up test infrastructure (temporary HTTP listeners on node3:8080/23, killed afterward at cmd-3135d5830db74e0d and cmd-10589e4e32154273). One self-corrected mistake occurred: an initial file-based reload of /etc/antrieb-acl.nft (cmd-06fa3e434ae84f4e, cmd-082d307a547c4676) duplicated forward-chain rules alongside the already-loaded runtime table; this was promptly diagnosed and fixed with an idempotent delete+define pattern (cmd-9a1c8c0aa812427a, cmd-19148a9385424be3), leaving no duplicate rules in the final state. A lower-risk, less clearly justified mutation is the removal of docker0's stale 240.127.1.1/24 address and bringing the interface down on node1 (cmd-9b725038c85341d3); this was not obviously required to satisfy the routing/ACL outcome and was not reverted, though it is low-risk (an unused/no-carrier interface) and matches pre-existing SONiC housekeeping guidance. Minor residue: node3 after-executor snapshot shows leftover /tmp/srv8080.log and /tmp/srv23.log test-server log files that were not cleaned up alongside the killed processes.
